description:
An open-source alternative to Claude Cowork, powered by OpenCode

OpenWork is an extensible, open-source “Claude Work” style system for knowledge workers.
It’s a native desktop app that runs OpenCode under the hood, but presents it as a clean, guided workflow:
- pick a workspace
- start a run
- watch progress + plan updates
- approve permissions when needed
- reuse what works (templates + skills)
The goal: make “agentic work” feel like a product, not a terminal.
Find shared connectors that still need your sign-in
- Shared connectors are easier to find. The Library now has a “Needs sign-in” filter for connectors shared with you that still need your sign-in. In Den, a sidebar dot also points out when something is waiting on you.
- Self-hosted first runs are faster. For self-hosters: openwork-server web opens your first folder in about a second on a fresh install, instead of taking 10+ seconds on Windows. It also no longer fails with “resource busy or locked” while installing the engine.
- Side chats no longer crowd the sidebar. Their chips have been removed from session rows, leaving more room for session names. Open a session to see its side chat.
Full changelog: https://openworklabs.com/docs/changelog · Compare
Windows installers are signed using Microsoft Artifact Signing.
